BURSEVI:v5p182/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p182/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p182/r1.claim: The years clarify the youths' counted time in the cave while alive and asleep. The phrase is apposition, not a specification; the latter parse would imply 600 years under al-Khalīl or 900 under the usual plural minimum.
BURSEVI:v5p182/r1.anchor: عطف بيان لثلاثمائة لا تمييز وإلا لكان أقل مدة لبثهم عند الخليل ستمائة سنة

BURSEVI:v5p182/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p182/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p182/r2.claim: On the tanwīn reading of مائة, the genitive plural follows; on the possessive reading, a plural stands for a singular, as in أعمالا.
BURSEVI:v5p182/r2.anchor: هذا على قراءة مائة بالتنوين وأما على قراءة الإضافة فأقيم الجمع مقام المفرد

BURSEVI:v5p182/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p182/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p182/r3.claim: The extra nine years convert the People of the Book's solar reckoning to the Arabs' lunar reckoning, with three years' difference per century; the source gives the lengths of solar and lunar years.
BURSEVI:v5p182/r3.anchor: أي : تسع سنين وهو إشارة إلى أن ذلك الحساب على اعتقاد أهل الكتاب شمسي

BURSEVI:v5p182/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p182/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p182/r4.claim: He calculates 300 solar years as 309 lunar years plus two months and nine days.
BURSEVI:v5p182/r4.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (وبتحقيق سيصدسال شمسي سيصدونه سال قمري ودوماه نوازده روز باشد)

QASHANI:18:25-26/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:25-26/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:25-26/r1.claim: The three hundred lunar-cycle years amount to twenty-five years, the time until the sleepers awoke; the added nine is the gestation period.
QASHANI:18:25-26/r1.anchor: من التي تبتنى على دور القمر فتكون كل سنة شهرا ومجموعها خمسة وعشرون سنة

QASHANI:18:25-26/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:25-26/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:25-26/r2.claim: The phrasing avoids calling the total 309 years: it leaves the counted unit ambiguous because ordinary usage at revelation meant solar years, allowing the unit to be months.
QASHANI:18:25-26/r2.anchor: لم يقل ثلثمائة سنة وتسعا، أو ثلثمائة وتسع سنين، لاستعمال السنة في العرف

QASHANI:18:25-26/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:25-26/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:25-26/r3.claim: The years remain indefinite in the wording; this supports the statement that God knows best how long they stayed.
QASHANI:18:25-26/r3.anchor: ثم بين أن المدة سنين مبهمة غير معينة، إذ لو قيل

QASHANI:18:25-26/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:25-26/r4.speaker: قتادة
QASHANI:18:25-26/r4.claim: Qatada says the duration is a continuation of the People of the Book’s reported claim, which the command that God knows best rejects.
QASHANI:18:25-26/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو حكاية كلام أهل الكتاب من تتمة سيقولون: وقوله: { قل الله أعلم } رد عليهم

QASHANI:18:25-26/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:25-26/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:25-26/r5.claim: A version of ʿAbd Allāh’s codex reads “and they said they stayed”; the duration is not certain or consistently established.
QASHANI:18:25-26/r5.anchor: أن اليقين غير محقق ولا مطرد

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p136/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p136/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p136/r1.claim: They read ثلاث مائة سنين with tanwin, while Hamza and al-Kisai make it a construct without tanwin.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p136/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم ثلاث مائة سنين منون

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p136/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p136/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p136/r2.claim: Abu al-Hasan says the years belong to the three hundred; although العرب rarely add مائة to plural سنين, the construction is permissible, and Ibn Masud's codex has سنة singular.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p136/r2.anchor: ولا يحسن إضافة المائة إلى السنين، لا تكاد العرب تقول: مائة سنين

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p136/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p136/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p136/r3.claim: The tanwin reading is sound because hundreds are usually annexed to singulars but can also be followed by plurals, as a cited poem demonstrates.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p136/r3.anchor: أن هذا الضرب من العدد الذي يضاف في اللغة المشهورة إلى الآحاد

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r1.claim: Tanwīn on مائة makes سنين an accusative governed by لبثوا and either a substitute for the number or its explanation; the alternative makes the number the object and سنين its substitute or explanation.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن اثبت التنوين أنه نصب سنين بقوله ولبثوا ثم أبدل ثلثمائة منها

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r2.claim: Idāfa gives the number its usual construction with a plural explanation; سنين is a sound plural with fatḥa on its nūn, and some Arabs inflect it like place names ending in yāʾ and nūn.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p223/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن أضاف أنه أتى بالعدد على وجهه وأضافه على خفة بالمفسر مجموعا على أصله

IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r1.claim: These readers use tanwīn in ثلث مائة سنين; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use idāfa without tanwīn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p389/r1.anchor: وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر / ثلث مائة سنين / منونا

QIRAAT-ER:18:25:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:25:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:25:5#1/r1.claim: The standard reading has tanwīn on miʾatin in an unusual construct, with sinīn as apposition or explanatory specification.
QIRAAT-ER:18:25:5#1/r1.anchor: Standard reading with tanwīn on miʾatin — thalātha and miʾatin are in construct

QIRAAT-ER:18:25:5#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:25:5#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:25:5#2/r1.claim: Without tanwīn, miʾati is mudāf and sinīn its genitive complement, forming a tighter unit.
QIRAAT-ER:18:25:5#2/r1.anchor: Without tanwīn on miʾati — standard iḍāfa construction where miʾati is mudāf and sinīn is mudāf ilayhi

QIRAAT-ER:18:25:5#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:25:5#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:25:5#3/r1.claim: The form miyatin drops hamza as a dialectal pronunciation without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:18:25:5#3/r1.anchor: Variant without hamza in miʾa — dialectal pronunciation miyah instead of miʾah

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#2/r1.claim: Qatada says Ibn Masud's reading includes وقالوا, making the people the ones who state the sleepers stayed three hundred years and nine; the command to say God knows best supports this reading.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p402#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولبثوا في كهفهم ﴾ قال في حرف ابن مسعود وقالوا ولبثوا يعني أنه قاله الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r4.claim: The three hundred plus nine years are God’s report of the youths’ sleep in the cave until their discovery; Mujāhid sees this as specifying the ‘counted years’ of 18:11.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r4.anchor: الظاهر أن قوله ولبثوا الآية إخبار من الله تعالى بمدة لبثهم نياما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r5.claim: After giving the exact duration, God commands the Prophet to say that God knows best: this is certain truth because God knows the unseen of heaven and earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r5.anchor: ولما تحرر هذا العدد بإخبار من الله تعالى أمر نبيه أن يقول قل الله أعلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r7.claim: The suggestion that the additional nine means hours, days, months, or years, disputed by Israelites, is far-fetched: an unspecified addition after a specified number inherits the same unit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r7.anchor: وهذا بعيد لأنه إذا سبق عدد مفسر وعطف عليه ما لم يفسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r8.speaker: النقاش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r8.claim: Al-Naqqāsh says the three hundred are solar years, with nine added because Arabs reckon lunar years, aligning the two calendars.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r8.anchor: وحكى النقاش أنها ثلاثمائة شمسية، ولما كان الخطاب للعرب زيدت التسع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r9.speaker: قتادة ومطر الوراق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r9.claim: Qatāda and Maṭar al-Warrāq say لبثوا is a report from the Israelites, citing ʿAbd Allāh’s codex; in the common reading it continues the people’s reported claims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p163/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة ومطر الوراق: لبثوا إخبار من بني إسرائيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r1.claim: One view says the Prophet is told to return knowledge of the duration to God, refuting others; Abū Ḥayyān prefers that the phrase belongs to the disputants, as the context indicates and because the matter is among God’s hidden knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r1.anchor: قيل: هو من قول المتنازعين في أمرهم وهو الصحيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says مائة with tanwīn is apposition or بدل بيان; others call it explanatory or a specification, and al-Zamakhsharī calls it apposition to ثلاثمائة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: على البدل أو عطف البيان. وقيل: على التفسير والتمييز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r3.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ reports allowing مائة as a substitute for مائة understood as ‘hundreds,’ but Abū Ḥayyān says Basrans reject apposition and that مائة normally takes a singular genitive, not plural سنين.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r3.anchor: فأما عطف البيان فلا يجوز على مذهب البصريين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وطلحة ويحيى والأعمش والحسن وابن أبي ليلى وخلف وابن سعدان وابن عيسى الأصبهاني وابن جبير الأنطاكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r4.claim: These readers omit tanwīn from مائة and attach it to سنين, using a plural where singular is usual; Abū Ḥātim harshly criticized the reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r4.anchor: مائة بغير تنوين مضافا إلى سنين أوقع الجمع موقع المفرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r5.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r5.claim: Abū ʿAlī says مائة is usually followed by a singular but may also be followed by a plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r5.anchor: وقال أبو علي: هذه تضاف في المشهور إلى المفرد، وقد تضاف إلى الجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r6.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r6.claim: Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh’s codex read سنة in the singular.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبي سنة وكذا في مصحف عبد الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r7.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reads سنون with wāw, supplied as a predicate: ‘they are years.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r7.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك: سنون بالواو على إضمار هي سنون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r8.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan and a narration from Abū ʿAmr pronounce تسعا with open tāʾ, like عشر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p164/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو عمرو في رواية اللؤلؤي عنه تسعا بفتح التاء

AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r2.claim: سنين may be a substitute for ثلاث or for مئة; it is genitive if it explains مئة and accusative if it explains ثلاث.
AKHFASH:v2p429#2/r2.anchor: على البدل من {ثلاث} ومن "المئة" أي: لبثوا ثلاث مئة

FARRA:v2p138/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p138/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p138/r4.claim: ثلاث مائة سنين is annexed in one analysis; other readers treat سنين as an accusative duration with لبثوا, or as a plural in place of سنة and explanatory accusative when nunated.
FARRA:v2p138/r4.anchor: وقوله: ثلاث مائة سنين [25] مضافة . وقد قرأ كثير من القراء

FARRA:v2p138/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p138/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p138/r5.claim: The poem about forty-two milking camels uses the plural سودا as an explanatory count-word, supporting the construction with سنين.
FARRA:v2p138/r5.anchor: فيها اثنتان وأربعون حلوبة ... سودا كخافية الغراب الأسحم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#2/r1.claim: After the number three hundred, sinīn clarifies the unit: three hundred years, not months or days, unlike a measure such as three hundred dirhams.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#2/r1.anchor: {ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين} ولم يقل: سنة. كأنه قال: ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاثمائة. ثم قال: سنين.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports that the verse first said three hundred; people asked whether days, months, or years, and then “years and nine more” was revealed.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p266#2/r2.anchor: وروى ابن فضيل عن الأجلح، عن الضحاك، قال: نزلت "ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة".

ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#2/r1.claim: The statement that the youths stayed three hundred years and nine more is an independent sentence explaining the earlier summary that God kept them asleep for a number of years; Mujāhid is cited for this explanation, which several scholars choose.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#2/r1.anchor: وهي جملة مستأنفة مبينة كما قال مجاهد لما أجمل في قوله تعالى ( فضربنا على آذانهم في الكهف سنين عددا )

ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r2.claim: The nine years may reconcile the solar-year count of the People of Scripture with the lunar-year count of Arabs, and this explanation is attributed by some to ʿAlī; al-Ālūsī details astronomical objections to the claimed nine-year difference.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r2.anchor: فقيل هو الإشارة إلى أنها ثلثمائة بحساب أهل الكتاب واعتبار السنة الشمسية وثلثمائة وتسع بحساب العرب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r3.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r3.claim: Al-Khafājī says the two counts are explicit in context: three hundred by the People of the Book's reckoning, then nine extra by the questioners' reckoning; the difference is approximate because the remaining fraction is below half a year.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r3.anchor: وبحث فيه الخفاجي بأن وجه الدلالة فيه ظاهر لأن المعنى لبثوا ثلثمائة سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r4.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r4.claim: Al-Ṭībī proposes that the sleepers nearly awoke after three hundred years but something kept them sleeping nine additional years; al-Ālūsī objects that the verse would then need to say their sleep increased.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r4.anchor: وقال الطيبي في توجيه العدول : إنه يمكن أن يقال : لعلهم لما استكملوا ثلثمائة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the nine-year sleep-extension proposal because it would require an unexpressed meaning, that their sleep itself grew stronger for nine years.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p251#3/r5.anchor: وتعقب بأن هذا يقتضي أن يكون المراد وازدادوا نوما أي قوى نومهم في تسع سنين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r1.claim: Some say the People of the Book disagreed over the sleepers' duration as they did their number; the verse resolves the disagreement, and the nine-year phrase confirms the answer like the exception in the account of Noah's thousand years.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r1.anchor: وقال أيضا : يجوز أن يكون أهل الكتاب قد اختلفوا في مدة لبثهم كما اختلفوا في عدتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r2.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r2.claim: Another view says the sleepers briefly awoke and then returned to sleep, explaining the increase; al-Ālūsī considers this closer than the solar-versus-lunar reckoning explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r2.anchor: وقيل إنهم انتبهوا قليلا ثم ردوا إلى حالتهم الأولى فلذا ذكر الازدياد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r3.claim: A view attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās treats the duration statement as the People of the Book's quoted speculation, not God's assertion; he argues that a true duration would not be followed by saying God knows best, and cites the prior reports as conjecture.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r3.anchor: ونسب ذلك إلى ابن عباس فقد أخرج ابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه عنه رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه قال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī doubts this attribution: Ibn ʿAbbās accepted the seven-sleepers view even though it too is followed by God's knowing their number, so the same wording cannot distinguish rejection here.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r4.anchor: فقد صح عنه القول بأن عدة أصحاب الكهف سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم مع أنه تعالى عقب القول بذلك بقوله سبحانه ( قل ربي أعلم بعدتهم )

ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's reading says that people said they remained in the cave, supporting the possibility that the duration is quoted speculation; al-Ālūsī still says the following divine statement does not by itself signal rejection.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p252/r5.anchor: نعم قرأ ابن مسعود ( قالوا لبثوا كهفهم ) وهو يقتضي أن يكون من كلام الخائضين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r1.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r1.claim: On the quoted-speech interpretation, al-Khafājī assigns the pronoun in “they increased” to the People of the Book: some said three hundred, others added nine; al-Ālūsī rejects this as weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r1.anchor: وقال الخفاجي : إن ضمير عليه لأهل الكتاب بخلافه على الأول ويظهر فيه وجه العدول

ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the suggestion that the nine is unspecified as to years, months, days, or hours: a following unqualified count takes the unit of the preceding explicit number.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r2.anchor: وقيل إنه تعالى ما قال ( وازدادوا تسعا ) كانت التسع مبهمة لا يدري أنها سنون أم شهور

ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r3.claim: The accusative “nine” is the one object of the verb “increased”; although Abū al-Baqāʾ says “increase” can take two objects, its derived form here takes one, as usage reported by al-Rāghib also supports.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r3.anchor: ونصب ( تسعا ) على أنه مفعول ( ازدادوا ) وهو مما يتعدى إلى واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn al-Ḥājib parse “years” in the common reading as an accusative substitute for “three hundred”; al-Zamakhsharī instead calls it an explanatory apposition, which the Sea commentary rejects for Basran grammar.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r4.anchor: فقال أبو البقاء وابن الحاجب : هو منصوب على البدلية من ( ثلثمائة )

ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r5.claim: Some prefer explanatory apposition because substitution would seem to make the number itself unintended; a report says listeners asked whether the three hundred meant days, months, or years, after which “years” was revealed. Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows either parsing.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r5.anchor: وادعى بعضهم أنه أولى من البدلية لأنها تستلزم أن لا يكون العدد مقصودا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r6.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r6.claim: A parsing of “years” as a numeral specification is criticized because it seems to make the stay nine hundred years: the specification should count one item per hundred, and years are plural; al-Ālūsī replies that plural specification follows the underlying collective usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r6.anchor: وقيل : على التمييز وتعقب بأنه يلزم عليه الشذوذ من وجهين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r7.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj also allows “years” to modify “hundred” in the genitive, semantically describing the whole number as in an Antarah verse about forty-two milk-camels; the passage continues its grammatical defense in the next segment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p253/r7.anchor: وجوز الزجاج كون ( سنين ) مجرورا على أنه نعت ( مائة ) وهو راجع في المعنى إلى جملة العدد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r1.speaker: أبو علي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r1.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains the poetic construction by taking “milch-camel” collectively, allowing its plural adjective to describe the whole numbered group; a collective plural in singular form can specify a numeral, as in “twenty persons.”
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r1.anchor: وقال أبو علي : لا يمتنع أن يكون الشاعر اعتبر حلوبة جمعا وجعل سودا وصفا لها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r2.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and several others recite “three hundred years” with “years” genitive by annexation; the same objection about making the duration nine hundred would apply only if it were a numeral specification.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وطلحة ويحيى والأعمش والحسن وابن أبي ليلى وخلف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r3.claim: The plural genitive is possible though uncommon: the plural ending may function like a replacement for the singular's deleted final consonant, and the Quranic reading itself suffices as Arabic evidence despite the lack of another attested example.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r3.anchor: لكن قالوا : إن الجمع المذكور فيها قد أجرى مجرى العاري عن علامة الجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r4.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r4.claim: Ubayy reads “three hundred year” with the singular genitive, the usual construction, as does the Ibn Masʿūd codex.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( ثلثمائة سنة ) بالإضافة والإفراد كما هو الاستعمال الشائع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r5.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reads “three hundred years” with the nominative plural, understood as the predicate of an omitted “they are.”
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r5.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك ( ثلثمائة سنون ) بالتنوين ورفع سنون على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r6.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAmr, in the narration of al-Luʾluʾī, read “nine” with an open tāʾ, a dialectal form.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p254/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو عمرو في رواية اللؤلؤي عنه ( تسعا ) بفتح التاء وهو لغة فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r4.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r4.claim: Some allegorize the three hundred and nine years as twenty-five years by treating a Quranic year as a month; al-Ālūsī rejects this as baseless, contrary to Muslim consensus and weak in faith, insisting the possible outward duration should stand.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r4.anchor: زعم بعض أهل التأويل أن مجموع ذلك خمس وعشرون سنة واعتبر السنة التي في الآية شهرا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r5.speaker: ابن سينا
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī supports the possibility of the long sleep by citing Ibn Sīnā's report that Aristotle described mystics who experienced a state resembling the cave sleepers before their time.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r5.anchor: ومما يدل على إمكان هذا اللبث أن أبا علي بن سينا ذكر في الباب الزمان من الشفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r6.claim: An allegory says direct divine training without shaykhs may take many years, while guidance through them may be completed in forty days or even a few days; al-Ālūsī answers that God can guide without intermediaries in a few hours.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p261/r6.anchor: وفي الآية على ما قيل إشارة إلى أن المزيد الذي يربيه الله سبحانه بلا واسطة المشايخ يصل في مدة مديدة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164#2/r1.claim: He says the three hundred years were what the People of the Book claimed, not a report from God; Ibn Masud's reading says 'they said.'
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم: هذا خبر عن أهل الكتاب أنهم قالوا ذلك. ولو كان خبرا من الله عز وجل عن قدر لبثهم لم يكن لقوله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164#2/r2.claim: Baghawī prefers the view that God himself reports the duration; God's knowing best answers disputants because He has disclosed it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164#2/r2.anchor: وقال الآخرون: هذا إخبار من الله تعالى عن قدر لبثهم في الكهف وهو الأصح.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164#2/r3.claim: Another account says the People of the Book counted from entry into the cave until their own time, while God's answer concerns the period after their souls were taken, known only to Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p164#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: إن أهل الكتاب قالوا: إن هذه المدة من لدن دخلوا الكهف إلى يومنا هذا ثلثمائة وتسع سنين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r1.claim: They read thalāthumiʾatin without tanwīn; the others use tanwīn.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي "ثلثمائة" بلا تنوين وقرأ الآخرون بالتنوين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r2.claim: The plural sinīn is explained as a later clarification after listeners asked whether the three hundred meant days, months, or years.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r2.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: "ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلثمائة" فقالوا: أياما أو شهورا أو سنين؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r3.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r3.claim: Some Arabs use sinīn in the place of sana, one year.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: ومن العرب من يضع سنين في موضع سنة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r4.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r4.claim: The Christians of Najran said they understood the three hundred but not the extra nine, so the latter was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p165/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي (2) قالت نصارى نجران أما ثلثمائة فقد عرفنا وأما التسع فلا علم لنا بها فنزلت

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:25/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:25/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:25/r1.claim: The three hundred years plus nine describe the time they remained alive and asleep, clarifying the earlier summary.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:25/r1.anchor: يعني لبثهم فيه أحياء مضروبا على آذانهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:25/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:25/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:25/r2.claim: Alternatively, the number quotes People of the Book traditions, among whom some said three hundred years and others three hundred and nine.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:25/r2.anchor: وقيل إنه حكاية كلام أهل الكتاب فإنهم اختلفوا في مدة لبثهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:25/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:25/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:25/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i link three hundred directly with years; the plural can stand for a singular, while unlinked years are appositional.

NAHHAS:v2p453/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r3.speaker: أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو وعاصم
NAHHAS:v2p453/r3.claim: They read the duration with tanwīn on miʾa; the Kufans except ʿĀṣim omit it.
NAHHAS:v2p453/r3.anchor: هذه قراءة أهل المدينة وأبي عمرو وعاصم ، وقرأ أهل الكوفة إلا عاصما ^ ( ثلاث مائة سنين ) ^ بغير تنوين

NAHHAS:v2p453/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p453/r4.claim: In the first reading, sinīn may be accusative as an appositional substitute for thalāth, or genitive after miʾa understood as a plural.
NAHHAS:v2p453/r4.anchor: القراءة الأولى على أن سنين في موضع نصب أو خفض ؛ فالنصب على البدل من ثلاث

NAHHAS:v2p453/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p453/r5.claim: He parses sinīn as an accusative of apposition and emphasis.
NAHHAS:v2p453/r5.anchor: وقال أبو اسحاق : سنين في موضع

NAHHAS:v2p453/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r6.speaker: الكسائي والفراء وأبو عبيدة
NAHHAS:v2p453/r6.claim: They construe the word order as ‘they remained years, three hundred.’
NAHHAS:v2p453/r6.anchor: وقال الكسائي والفراء وأبو عبيدة : التقدير ولبثوا في كهفهم سنين ثلاث مئة

NAHHAS:v2p453/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p453/r7.claim: The genitive links years to miʾa as if it meant hundreds; the cited poem likewise uses a singular noun as a plural in sense.
NAHHAS:v2p453/r7.anchor: والخفض رد على مئة لأنها بمعنى مئين ، كما أنشد النحويون

NAHHAS:v2p453/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p453/r8.claim: The uninflected ‘three hundred years’ construction is remote Arabic and should be avoided in recitation; idiomatic Arabic says three hundred year, with the singular carrying plural sense.
NAHHAS:v2p453/r8.anchor: فأما ثلاث مئة سنين فبعيد في العربية . يجب أن تتوقى القراءة به ؛ لأن كلام العرب ثلاث مئة سنة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r1.claim: The three hundred years are solar years, using the reckoning of the Jewish questioners; the wording also alludes to the era's unbelieving rule and persecution.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r1.anchor: شمسية بحساب اليهود الآمرين بهذا السؤال , وعبر بلفظ السنة إشارة إلى ذمها وقع فيها من علو أهل الكفر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r2.claim: The added nine years are lunar, converting the three hundred solar years to the Arabs' lunar reckoning based on the difference between year lengths.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p461/r2.anchor: لأن تفاوت ما بين السنة الشمسية والقمرية عشرة أيام وإحدى وعشرون ساعة وخمسا ساعة

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r10.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r10.claim: Uthman recited the word سنين in the duration verse with nunation.
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r10.anchor: عن حكيم بن عقال قال: سمعت عثمان بن عفان يقرأ: {ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين} منونة

DURR-FULL:v5p378/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas warns that an interpreter may stray vastly from the truth by treating the reported duration as God's own statement.
DURR-FULL:v5p378/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن الرجل ليفسر الآية يرى أنها كذلك فيهوي أبعد ما بين السماء والأرض

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says 309 years is what people reported, not God's own assertion; otherwise God would not have said that He knows best how long they remained.
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r1.anchor: ثم قال: كم لبث القوم قالوا: ثلاثمائة وتسع سنين قال: لو كانوا لبثوا كذلك لم يقل الله: {قل الله أعلم بما لبثوا}

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r2.claim: The Ibn Masud reading says people reported the 300 years; Qatada cites God's command to say that He knows best as confirmation.
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في حرف ابن مسعود وقالوا لبثوا في كهفهم الآية يعني إنما قاله الناس

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r3.claim: Qatada says the 300 years and nine is the People of the Book's statement, which God answers by saying He knows best.
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا} قال: هذا قول أهل الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r4.claim: When people asked whether the duration was days, months, or years, the verse specifying years and nine more was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية {في كهفهم ثلاث مائة} قيل: يا رسول الله أياما أم شهورا أم سنين

DURR-FULL:v5p379/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r5.claim: Mujahid explains 300 years and nine more as the count of their stay.
DURR-FULL:v5p379/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا} يقول: عدد ما لبثوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r1.claim: The clause may continue what people say after 18:22, meaning they say the sleepers remained 309 years; Ibn Masʿūd’s reading ‘and they said’ supports this attachment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r1.anchor: فيجوز أن تكون جملة ولبثوا } عطفا على مقولهم في قوله : { سيقولون ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم . ( الكهف : 22 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd read ‘and they said they remained in their cave,’ clarifying the interpretation that the duration is reported speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r2.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود أنه قرأ وقالوا لبثوا في كهفهم } إلى آخره ، فذلك تفسير لهذا العطف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the clause may continue the whole narrative as God’s statement that they remained in the cave for 309 years.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون العطف على القصة كلها . والتقدير : وكذلك أعثرنا عليهم إلى آخره ، وهم لبثوا في كهفهم ثلاثمائة سنة وتسع سنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r4.claim: The apparent meaning is the sleepers’ first interval before awakening, matching the earlier discussion of how long they slept; Christian historians instead claimed 240 years.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r4.anchor: ثم إن الظاهر أن القرآن أخبر بمدة لبث أهل الكهف في كهفهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r5.claim: Another proposed meaning is the period from their final death until the verse’s revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : المراد لبثهم من وقت موتهم الأخير إلى زمن نزول هذه الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r6.claim: The 309 years express 300 solar years plus nine lunar years, aligning the Roman calendar with the lunar years used by Arabs and Muslims; a full lunar year accrues per 33 solar years.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r6.anchor: فعبر عن هذا العدد بأنه ثلاثمائة سنة وزيادة تسع ، ليعلم أن التقدير بالسنين القمرية المناسبة لتاريخ العرب والإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r7.speaker: السهيلي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r7.claim: Al-Suhaylī says Christians knew the sleepers’ story and dated events by it; Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmits from al-Naqqāsh the calculation that 100 solar years differ by three lunar years.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r7.anchor: قال السهيلي في الروض الأنف } : النصارى يعرفون حديث أهل الكهف ويؤرخون به . وأقول : واليهود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r8.claim: Ibn Ashur presents the lunar-solar conversion as a scientific aspect of Qur’anic inimitability beyond the general knowledge of Arabs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p300#2/r8.anchor: وبهذا تظهر نكتة التعبير عن التسع السنين بالازدياد . وهذا من علم القرآن وإعجازه العلمي الذي لم يكن لعموم العرب علم به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301/r1.claim: The majority read miʾah with tanwīn; sinīn is either apposition under the view that one hundred cannot take an accusative specification, or a specification for those who allow it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { ثلاث مائة } بالتنوين . وانتصب { سنين } على البدلية من اسم العدد على رأي من يمنع مجيء تمييز المائة منصوبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301/r2.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read miʾata sinīna in annexation; a plural specification after one hundred is rare but eloquent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p301/r2.anchor: وقرأه حمزة والكسائي وخلف بإضافة مائة إلى سنين على أنه تمييز للمائة . وقد جاء تمييز المائة جمعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r1.speaker: قتادة ومطر الوراق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r1.claim: Qatada and Matar al-Warraq say the statement about three hundred years is a quotation of what the Israelites said, citing Ibn Masud's codex wording 'and they said'; Qatada takes that phrase as attached to the earlier reported claims.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r1.anchor: قال قتادة ومطر الوراق وغيرهما ولبثوا في كهفهم الآية حكاية عن بني إسرائيل أنهم قالوا ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r7.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r7.claim: Al-Naqqash explains the nine-year difference as converting three hundred solar years into the equivalent lunar count used by the Arab audience.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r7.anchor: وحكى النقاش ما معناه: أنهم لبثوا ثلاثمائة سنة شمسية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r8.claim: They apparently entered the cave shortly after Jesus, while some of his disciples were still alive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r8.anchor: والظاهر من أمرهم أنهم قاموا ودخلوا الكهف بعد عيسى بيسير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r9.claim: Most readers put tanwin on miʾa and treat sinin as a substitute, explanatory apposition, or specification; Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, Yahya, Talha, and al-Aʿmash attach miʾa to sinin without tanwin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p509#3/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «ثلاثمائة سنين» بتنوين مائة ونصب «سنين»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r1.claim: The continuation gives Ibn Masud's codex reading as 'three hundred years'; al-Dahhak has a plural reading and Abu Amr a vowel variant.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r6.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says people first asked whether the three hundred meant months, days, or years, after which the words 'years and nine more' were revealed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p510/r6.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن الضحاك بن مزاحم أنه قال: نزلت هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r1.claim: They read ثلاثمائة سنين with nunation on the number.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر ثلاثمائة سنين منونا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r2.claim: They read ثلاثمائة سنين as an annexation, without nunation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي ثلاثمائمة سنين مضافا غير منون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r3.claim: A number attached to units may be annexed to a plural; he cites poetry with خمسمئ منها قسي as evidence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي العدد المضاف إلى الآحاد قد جاء مضافا إلى الجميع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r4.claim: One view treats three hundred years as what people said about the youths, not the actual period; Ibn Abbas argues the following statement that God knows best would otherwise be odd, and Qatada agrees.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r4.anchor: أحدهما أنه حكاية عما قال الناس في حقهم وليس بمقدار لبثهم قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r5.speaker: عبيد بن عمير ومجاهد والضحاك وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r5.claim: Another view takes the three hundred years as the actual time from entering the cave until God raised them and disclosed them to people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r5.anchor: والثاني أنه مقدار ما لبثوا قاله عبيد بن عمير ومجاهد والضحاك وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r6.speaker: الفراء وأبو عبيدة والكسائي والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r6.claim: They supply an implied construction: three hundred years of years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r6.anchor: قال الفراء وأبو عبيدة والكسائي والزجاج التقدير سنين ثلاثمائة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r7.claim: The wording specifies years rather than months or days.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة المعنى أنها لم تكن شهورا ولا أياما وإنما كانت سنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r8.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r8.claim: He parses سنين as an appositive to ثلاثمائة.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي سنين بدل من قوله ثلاثمائة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r9.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r9.claim: He says the clarification سنين was revealed after people wondered whether the three hundred were days, months, or years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r9.anchor: قال الضحاك نزلت ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاثمائة فقالوا أياما أو شهورا أو سنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r10.claim: Nine years are added; the word years is omitted because it was already stated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p130#2/r10.anchor: وازدادوا تسعا يعني تسع سنين فاستغنى عن ذكر السنين بما تقدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r1.claim: God reports that the Sleepers remained three hundred lunar years plus nine, which equals three hundred solar years because each century differs by three years in the two calendars.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r1.anchor: وأنه كان مقداره ثلاثمائة [سنة] (6) وتسع سنين بالهلالية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r3.claim: Qatada, followed by Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah, says the three hundred years plus nine was the People of the Book's statement, rejected by the following command to say God knows; he cites a variant reading attributed to Ibn Masud, وقالوا ولبثوا.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا} هذا قول أهل الكتاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects Qatada's attribution: the People of the Book give three hundred solar years without nine; the verse is God's own report, as Ibn Jarir also chose. The Ibn Masud reading has a disconnected transmission and is anomalous against the majority reading, so it is not evidence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p150#2/r4.anchor: وظاهر من الآية إنما هو إخبار من الله، لا حكاية عنهم. وهذا اختيار ابن جرير، رحمه الله.

JISHUMI:v6p4386/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r1.claim: They read ثلاث مائة سنين without tanwīn; the other readers use tanwīn, which the author prefers as the better Arabic construction.
JISHUMI:v6p4386/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: ثلاث مائة سنين بغير تنوين، والباقون بالتنوين وهو الاختيار في العربية

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r6.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r6.claim: One view attributes the 300 years and nine to the Jews or People of the Book; the answer ‘God knows best’ responds to their claim.
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r6.anchor: قيل: هذا خبر عن أهل الكتاب، وقيل: عن اليهود أنهم قالوا ذلك، ولذلك قال: (قل الله أعلم بما لبثوا)، عن قتادة،

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r7.speaker: مطر الوراق
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r7.claim: He says the Jews stated the duration and God answered them; Abū Muslim also allows this interpretation.
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r7.anchor: قال مطر الوراق: هذا شيء قالته اليهود فرد الله عليهم، وجوز أبو مسلم هذا الوجه،

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r8.claim: The author questions attributing the duration statement to the Jews without evidence, even while acknowledging that interpretation has an attractive aspect.
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r8.anchor: وقيل: هذا ليس بصحيح لأنه لا يجوز صرف كلامه تعالى إلى غيره إلا بدليل مع أن فيه وجه حسن،

JISHUMI:v6p4392/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r9.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
JISHUMI:v6p4392/r9.claim: They say God Himself reports that the youths remained in the cave for 300 years plus nine.

SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r1.speaker: الأخوان
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r1.claim: The two readers attach مئة to سنين; al-Zamakhshari explains the plural as standing for a singular, like أعمالا for عملا.
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r1.anchor: قرأ الأخوان بإضافة " مئة " إلى سنين.

SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r2.claim: Abu Hatim criticized the reading that annexes مئة to سنين.
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r2.anchor: وقد أنحى أبو حاتم على هذه القراءة

SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r3.claim: The author dismisses Abu Hatim's criticism of the annexed reading.

SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r4.speaker: عبد الله وأبي
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r4.claim: Ibn Masud's codex has singular سنة, and Ubayy read that form.
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r4.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله " سنة " بالإفراد.

SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r5.speaker: الضحاك
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak read سنون as a predicate of an omitted subject, meaning they are years.
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r5.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك " سنون " بالواو على أنها خبر مبتدأ مضمر، أي: هي سنون.

SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r6.claim: With the remaining reading, tanwin leaves سنين as بدل or عطف بيان for ثلثمئة; Abu al-Baqa allows بدل of مئة because it means a plural.
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r6.anchor: وجعلوا " سنين " بدلا من " ثلثمئة " أو عطف بيان.

SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r7.claim: سنين cannot be a classifier in this reading except by poetic necessity, and the cited verse uses a singular classifier.
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r7.anchor: ولا جائز أن يكون " سنين " في هذه القراءة مميزا، لأن ذلك إنما يجيء

SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r8.claim: تسعا means nine years; the classifier is omitted because the previous mention makes it clear, and تسعا is a direct object.
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r8.anchor: أي: تسع سنين، حذف المميز لدلالة ما تقدم عليه، إذ

SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r9.claim: ازداد is an iftiʿāl form with ta changed to dal after zay; the base verb takes two objects, while this derived form takes one fewer.
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r9.anchor: وازداد: افتعل، أبدلت التاء دالا بعد الزاي، وكان متعديا لاثنين

SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r10.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r10.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu Amr in one transmission read تسعا with fatḥa on tā, like عشر.
SAMIN-DURR:18:25/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو عمرو في وراية " تسعا " بفتح التاء كعشر.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r1.claim: The stated duration is the time they remained alive asleep in the cave, clarifying the earlier account of years spent under the sleep.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r1.anchor: يريد لبثهم فيه أحياء مضروبا على آذانهم هذه المدة ، وهو بيان لما أجمل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r4.claim: In the codex of ʿAbdullah, the wording includes “they say: they remained.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r4.anchor: وقال في حرف عبد الله : وقالوا لبثوا .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r5.claim: “Years” is an explanatory apposition to three hundred; a reading has the genitive construction with a plural in place of a singular measure, as in 18:103.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r5.anchor: وسنين : عطف بيان لثلثمائة . وقرىء ( ثلثمائة سنين ) ، بالإضافة ، على وضع الجمع موضع الواحد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r6.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r6.claim: Ubayy’s reading uses the singular “year” after three hundred.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r7.claim: “Nine” means nine years, supplied by the preceding duration.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p669#2/r7.anchor: تسعا } تسع سنين ؛ لأن ما قبله يدل عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r1.claim: In Ibn Masud's reading, they say that the youths remained three hundred years plus nine.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r1.anchor: في قراءة ابن مسعود قالوا لبثوا في كهفهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r2.speaker: يهود ونصارى نجران
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r2.claim: One view treats the three hundred years plus nine as a claim by Jews or the Christians of Najran, which God answers by saying that He knows best how long they stayed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r2.anchor: أن هذا قول اليهود , وقيل بل نصارى نجران أنهم لبثوا في كهفهم ثلاثمائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا , فرد الله تعالى عليهم قولهم وقال لنبيه { قل الله أعلم بما لبثوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r3.claim: Alternatively, God Himself reports the total time from their entry into the cave until their deaths.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r3.anchor: أن هذا إخبار من الله تعالى بهذا العدد عن مدة بقائهم في الكهف من حين دخلوه إلى ما ماتوا فيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r4.claim: The extra nine years account for the difference between solar and lunar years.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p299/r4.anchor: وازدادوا تسعا } هو ما بين السنين الشمسية والسنين القمرية

MUJAHID:v1p375#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p375#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p375#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says the number stated is the length of the youths' stay.
MUJAHID:v1p375#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا ﴾ يعني عدد ما لبثوا

MUQATIL:18:25-26/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:25-26/r1.speaker: النصارى
MUQATIL:18:25-26/r1.claim: The Christians also say that the youths slept in their cave for three hundred years plus nine.
MUQATIL:18:25-26/r1.anchor: قالت النصارى أيضا: { ولبثوا في كهفهم } رقودا، { ثلاث مئة سنين وازدادوا تسعا } [آية: 25]، فيها تقديم،

MUQATIL:18:25-26/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:25-26/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:25-26/r2.claim: The phrase has fronting, and the sleepers' colors, hair, and clothes did not change.
MUQATIL:18:25-26/r2.anchor: فيها تقديم، لا تتغير ألوانهم، ولا أشعارهم، ولا ثيابهم.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11/r1.claim: The three hundred years describe the time they remained alive while their hearing was sealed; this explains the earlier statement that God sealed their ears for years.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11/r1.anchor: يريد لبثهم فيه أحياء مضروبا على آذانهم هذه المدة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11/r2.claim: The genitive reading of “three hundred years” by Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim uses a plural where a singular would ordinarily serve as the number's specification.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11/r2.anchor: عطف بيان لثلثمائة ثلثمائة سنين بالإضافة حمزة وعلى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p11/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11/r3.claim: The nine are nine years, understood from the preceding number; azdādū takes one object because its base verb takes two.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p11/r3.anchor: أي تسع سنين لدلالة ما قبله عليه وتسعا مفعول به

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r1.claim: Ibn Masud's codex adds wa-qalu, 'and they said,' before the statement of duration.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r2.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r2.claim: Al-Tabari says Israelites disputed how long had passed since the youths were discovered; God clarifies that 300 years and nine describe their sleep, while the later period is unknown to humans.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r2.anchor: فأخبر الله تعالى نبيه أن هذه المدة في كونهم نياما

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r3.claim: On this reading, the first 'they remained' refers to sleep, and the second to the time after discovery until Muhammad's era or their bodies' decay.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية: فقوله على هذا «لبثوا» الأول

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r4.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r4.claim: Mujahid says their later, unspecified stay extended until the Qur'an was revealed.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r5.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says the later period extended until they died; another report says the nine's units were unclear to people, so knowledge was referred to God.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r6.claim: The apparent Arabic sense is nine years because years were just named; the historical appearance is that the youths entered the cave not long after Jesus while some disciples remained.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r6.anchor: وظاهر كلام العرب المفهوم منه أنها أعوام

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r7.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r7.claim: Al-Qushayri says the nine cannot mean nights or hours because the preceding word years supplies the understood unit, as in a hundred dirhams and five.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r7.anchor: لا يفهم من التسع تسع ليال وتسع ساعات لسبق ذكر السنين

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r8.speaker: أبو علي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r8.claim: Abu Ali supplies an omitted noun: they remained an additional nine years.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r8.anchor: وقال أبو علي «وازدادوا تسعا» أي ازدادوا لبث

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r9.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says listeners asked whether the 300 were years, months, weeks, or days, so God specified 'years.'
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r9.anchor: وقال الضحاك: لما نزلت { ولبثوا في كهفهم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r10.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r10.claim: Al-Naqqash explains nine as the difference between 300 solar years and their equivalent lunar years, about one year per 33⅓ solar years; al-Ghaznawi gives a similar account.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r10.anchor: لبثوا ثلثمائة سنة شمسية بحساب الأيام فلما كان الإخبار هنا للنبي العربي

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r11.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r11.claim: The majority read '300' with an indefinite hundred and accusative sinin, interpreting the order as '300 years'; sinin is apposition, explication, or specification.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r11.anchor: قرأ الجمهور «ثلثمائة سنين» بتنوين مائة ونصب سنين

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r12.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r12.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai join miʾa to sinin without tanwin, treating the plural as equivalent to singular sana.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r12.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بإضافة مائة إلى سنين، وترك التنوين

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r13.speaker: أبو علي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r13.claim: Abu Ali notes that numbers normally joined to singular nouns can also be joined to plurals; Ibn Masud's codex instead has '300 year.'
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r13.anchor: هذه الأعداد التي تضاف في المشهور إلى الآحاد نحو ثلثمائة رجل وثوب

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r14.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r14.claim: Al-Dahhak reads thalathamiʾata sunun with nominative plural ending.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r15.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r15.claim: Abu Amr has a variant reading of tisʿan with fatḥa on tāʾ; the majority use kasra.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r15.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بخلاف «تسعا» بفتح التاء وقرأ الجمهور بكسرها

QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r16.speaker: الفراء والكسائي وأبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r16.claim: They parse the construction in the order 'they remained years, three hundred.'
QURTUBI-FULL:18:25/r16.anchor: التقدير ولبثوا في كهفهم سنين ثلثمائة

ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r1.claim: سنين may be accusative as the time after the number, appositionally, or as an adjective of مائة; a poetic example makes an adjective describe a number in sense.
ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r1.anchor: جائز أن يكون (سنين) نصبا، وجائز أن تكون جرا.

ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r2.claim: The author prefers a report from God of the actual duration over the disputants' guesses, making the full number a stronger sign.
ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r2.anchor: ويجوز - وهو الأجود عندي - أنه إخبار عن الله أخبرهم بطول لبثهم.

ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r3.claim: The nine are not nine nights or hours: the number's unit need not be repeated once established.
ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r3.anchor: فلا يكون على معنى وازدادوا تسع ليال، ولا تسع ساعات،

ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r4.speaker: أبو العباس محمد بن يزيد
ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r4.claim: Abu al-Abbas explains ten as ten periods, each a day and night; Arabs count nights prominently, and the feminine form shows they are not months.
ZAJJAJ:v3p278/r4.anchor: قال أبو العباس محمد بن يزيد: (وعشرا) معناه وعشر مدد،

RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r8.claim: Some take the statement that the youths stayed 300 years as a quotation of what people say, supported by the reply that follows and a reading in ʿAbd Allāh's codex, “and they said.”
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r8.anchor: هو كلام الله تعالى فإنه أخبر عن كمية تلك المدة

RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r9.claim: Others take the 300-year statement as God's own report; the intervening prohibition of disputation separates it from the earlier quoted claims, and the reply directs people to God's knowledge rather than the People of the Book.
RAZI-FULL:v21p94/r9.anchor: هو كلام الله تعالى فإنه أخبر

RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r1.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read thalāth miʾat sinīn without tanwīn; the others use tanwīn. With tanwīn, sinīn is apposition explaining the unit, or the order is inverted to “years, three hundred.”
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي ثلثمائة سنين بغير تنوين والباقون بالتنوين

RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r2.claim: Under Ḥamza's reading, the normal construct would be “three hundred years,” but plural can stand in a specification where singular is expected, as in 18:103.
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r2.anchor: الواجب في الإضافة ثلثمائة سنة إلا أنه يجوز وضع الجمع موضع الواحد في التمييز

RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r3.claim: One explanation says 300 solar years equal 309 lunar years, though Rāzī says the arithmetic does not support it.
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r3.anchor: كانت المدة ثلثمائة سنة من السنين الشمسية وثلثمائة وتسع سنين من القمرية

RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r4.claim: Rāzī tentatively suggests that after completing 300 years, circumstances may have prolonged their sleep by nine more years.
RAZI-FULL:v21p95/r4.anchor: لعلهم لما استكملوا ثلثمائة سنة قرب أمرهم من الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r1.claim: One chronology places the Sleepers before Moses and says Moses mentioned them in the Torah, explaining why Jews asked about them.
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r1.anchor: قيل إنهم كانوا قبل موسى عليه السلام وإن موسى ذكرهم في التوراة

RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r2.claim: Another chronology says they entered the cave before Jesus, Jesus related their story, and they awoke between Jesus and Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r2.anchor: إنهم دخلوا الكهف قبل المسيح وأخبر المسيح بخبرهم ثم بعثوا في الوقت

RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r3.speaker: القفال عن محمد بن إسحاق
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r3.claim: Al-Qaffal attributes to Muhammad ibn Ishaq the view that the Sleepers entered the cave after Jesus.
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r3.anchor: وحكى القفال هذا القول عن محمد بن إسحاق

RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r4.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r4.claim: Some people claim the Sleepers never died and will remain alive until the Resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r4.anchor: إنهم لم يموتوا ولا يموتون إلى يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r5.speaker: محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r5.claim: Al-Khwarizmi says al-Wathiq sent him to the Romans to investigate the purported cave of the Sleepers.
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r5.anchor: أن الواثق أنفذه ليعرف حال أصحاب الكهف إلى الروم

RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r6.speaker: محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r6.claim: Al-Khwarizmi reports seeing hair on the bodies' chests and judging the display a contrivance, with corpses preserved against decay.
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r6.anchor: فدخلت ورأيت الشعور على صدورهم قال وعرفت أنه تمويه واحتيال

RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r7.speaker: محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r7.claim: The preserved bodies may have been treated with drying medicines such as aloe to prevent their decay.
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r7.anchor: عالجوا تلك الجثث بالأدوية المجففة لأبدان الموتى لتصونها عن البلى

RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r8.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r8.claim: Al-Qaffal says it is unknown whether the reported site is the actual cave or another place, and Roman identification is no proof.
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r8.anchor: والذي عندنا لا يعرف أن ذلك الموضع هو موضع أصحاب الكهف أو موضع آخر

RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r9.speaker: معاوية
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r9.claim: Al-Kashshaf relates that Muawiya passed the cave during a Roman campaign and wanted to uncover the Sleepers and see them.
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r9.anchor: ذكر في الكشاف عن معاوية أنه غزا الروم فمر بالكهف

RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas told Muawiya that God had forbidden him to inspect the Sleepers, as He had forbidden someone better than him.
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r10.anchor: ليس لك ذلك قد منع الله من هو خير منك

RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r11.speaker: معاوية
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r11.claim: In the report, Muawiya insisted on learning their condition and sent men into the cave; a divinely sent wind burned them.
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r11.anchor: فلما دخلوا الكهف بعث الله عليهم ريحا فأحرقتهم

RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r12.claim: Reason cannot establish the Sleepers' era or location; this knowledge requires a revealed text, which is unavailable.
RAZI-FULL:v21p96/r12.anchor: العلم بذلك الزمان وبذلك المكان ليس للعقل فيه مجال

RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r1.claim: Resurrection's possibility rests on God's power over all possible things, knowledge of all universals and particulars, and the possibility of what occurs once occurring at other times.
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r1.anchor: أنه تعالى قادر على كل الممكنات

RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r2.claim: Given those principles, sustaining a person safely through three hundred years of sleep is possible just as keeping someone alive during a day's sleep is possible.
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r2.anchor: فكذلك بقاؤه مدة ثلثمائة سنة يجب أن يكون ممكنا بمعنى أن إله العالم يحفظه

RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r3.speaker: الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r3.claim: Philosophers also allow that unusual celestial configurations could produce rare, extraordinary conditions in sublunary matter.
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r3.anchor: لا يبعد وقوع أشكال فلكية غريبة توجب في هيولي عالم الكون والفساد حصول أحوال غريبة نادرة

RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r4.claim: The neighboring surahs present three rare marvels: the bodily night journey, the Sleepers' long sleep, and Jesus' birth without a father.
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r4.anchor: هذه السور الثلاثة المتعاقبة اشتمل كل واحد منها على حصول حالة عجيبة نادرة

RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r5.claim: The stated argument from divine knowledge and power establishes the possibility of all three marvels.
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r5.anchor: والمعتمد في بيان إمكان كل هذه العجائب والغرائب المذكورة في هذه السور الثلاثة المتوالية

RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r6.speaker: أبو علي بن سينا عن أرسطاطاليس
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r6.claim: In the Shifa's discussion of time, Avicenna reports Aristotle's account of a group of godly people experiencing a state like the Sleepers.
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r6.anchor: أن أرسطاطاليس الحكيم ذكر أنه عرض لقوم من المتألهين حالة شبيهة بحالة أصحاب الكهف

RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r7.speaker: أبو علي بن سينا
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r7.claim: Avicenna says historical records indicate that those people lived before the Companions of the Cave.
RAZI-FULL:v21p97/r7.anchor: ويدل التاريخ على أنهم كانوا قبل أصحاب الكهف

STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r11.claim: The youths' centuries-long sleep represents an intermediate realm between life and death, analogous to the state between individual death and universal resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r11.anchor: their sleep represents an intermediate realm between life and death

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r1.claim: Some say the 309 years report the People of the Book’s reckoning, not necessarily the youths’ actual time in the cave; verse 26 then reserves knowledge to God.
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r1.anchor: said by some to be God’s informing the Prophet of the number of years the People of the Book say they remained in the cave

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r2.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r2.claim: Others take 309 years as the youths’ actual sleep in the cave and understand God knows best to concern the interval after their death, shortly after discovery.
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r2.anchor: Others claim that this figure represents the actual number of years the youths slept in the cave

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r3.speaker: still others
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r3.claim: Still others say 309 is the actual duration and settles the dispute about how long they remained.
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r3.anchor: Still others suggest that the figure of 309 years represents the actual number of years in the cave

STUDYQURAN:18:25/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r4.claim: Some explain 300 years by the solar calendar plus nine years to express the same period in the lunar calendar used by the Prophet and Arabs.
STUDYQURAN:18:25/r4.anchor: 300 years represents the amount of time they slept in the cave according to the solar calendar, and another 9 years would have to be added

ASAD-NOTES:18:25#n34/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:25#n34/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:25#n34/r1.claim: Asad reads the three hundred years and added nine as a report of idle guesses, refuted by God's statements in verses 22 and 26.
ASAD-NOTES:18:25#n34/r1.anchor: mentioned in the first paragraph of verse 22 above - guesses refuted by the subsequent statements

ASAD-NOTES:18:25#n34/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:25#n34/r2.speaker: Abd Allah ibn Masud, Qatadah, Matar al-Warraq
ASAD-NOTES:18:25#n34/r2.claim: These authorities treated the duration as something people said; Ibn Masud's Qur'an copy reportedly included that framing.
ASAD-NOTES:18:25#n34/r2.anchor: the view of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, whose copy of the Qur'an is said to have contained the words

ASAD-NOTES:18:25#n34/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:25#n34/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:25#n34/r3.claim: Asad's opening interpolation, some people asserted, follows qalu in Ibn Masud's marginal explanatory wording.
ASAD-NOTES:18:25#n34/r3.anchor: used by Ibn Mas'ud in his marginal note

TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says the statement that the youths stayed three hundred years and nine more is what the People of the Book say, and God corrects them in the next verse.
TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا} [الكهف: 25] هذا قول أهل الكتاب

TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r2.speaker: مطر الوراق
TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r2.claim: Maṭar al-Warrāq likewise says the duration was something Jews said, which God refuted by saying He knows best how long they remained.
TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r2.anchor: عن مطر الوراق، في قول الله: {ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين} [الكهف: 25] قال: إنما هو شيء

TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid takes the three hundred years and nine more as the number of years they actually remained.
TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين

TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr explicitly glosses the added nine as nine years.
TAB-FULL:v15p228#2/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير، قال: {ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا} [الكهف: 25] قال: وتسع سنين

TAB-FULL:v15p231/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r1.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says that after the verse first stated three hundred, people asked whether this meant days, months, or years, and the clarification came that it was years plus nine.
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم، قال: نزلت هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v15p231/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses their cave as lying between two mountains.
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، ولبثوا في كهفهم قال: بين جبلين

TAB-FULL:v15p231/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī holds that God states their actual stay: three hundred years and nine from entering the cave until He awakened and exposed them; the verse gives this directly.
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r3.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب أن يقال كما قال الله عز ذكره

TAB-FULL:v15p231/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r4.claim: He rejects treating 18:25 as an unmarked quotation of the People of the Book: the text gives no signal of reported speech, and a claim about God’s words needs proof.
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r4.anchor: ولم يضع دليلا على أن ذلك خبر منه عن قول قوم قالوه

TAB-FULL:v15p231/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r6.claim: Medinan, Basran, and some Kufan readers add tanwīn to three hundred and read the following word as an explanation; most Kufans construct the number directly with سنين.
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r6.anchor: فقرأت ذلك عامة قراء المدينة والبصرة وبعض الكوفيين {ثلاث مائة سنين} [الكهف: 25] بتنوين

TAB-FULL:v15p231/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers tanwīn because hundreds are normally explained by a singular noun; plural explanations occur, but less often.
TAB-FULL:v15p231/r7.anchor: وأولى القراءتين في ذلك عندي بالصواب قراءة من قرأه: {ثلاث مائة} [الكهف: 25] بالتنوين

TABATABAI:18:25-26/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r1.claim: The stated three hundred years plus nine gives the youths’ sleeping duration, first summarized as a number of years; the following verse and sequence support this duration as the true account.
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r1.anchor: بيان لمدة لبثهم في الكهف على حال النوم فإن هذا اللبث هو متعلق العناية في آيات القصة

TABATABAI:18:25-26/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r2.claim: The duration is not a quotation from the People of the Book refuted by the next verse, nor three hundred years from God with nine added by them; their reported figure was two hundred or less.
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r2.anchor: على أن المنقول عنهم أنهم قالوا بلبثهم مائتي سنة أو أقل لا ثلاثمائة وتسعة

TABATABAI:18:25-26/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r3.claim: Sinin is an appositional substitute for three hundred, not its numeral specification, which would be singular; plural wording may magnify the long duration.
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r3.anchor: ليس بمميز للعدد وإلا لقيل ثلاثمائة سنة

TABATABAI:18:25-26/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r4.claim: The added nine has an emphatic sense, as if to say not merely three hundred long years but nine more; the earlier account minimizes the period while this verse stresses its length.
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r4.anchor: كأنه قيل ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاثمائة سنة هذه السنين المتمادية والدهر الطويل بل ازدادوا تسعا

TABATABAI:18:25-26/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r5.claim: The nine-year difference indicates three hundred solar years equal roughly three hundred and nine lunar years; Quranic years are lunar, and approximate ratios need not match exactly.
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r5.anchor: إضافة تسع سنين إلى ثلاثمائة سنة مدة اللبث تعطي أنهم لبثوا في كهفهم ثلاثمائة سنة شمسية

TABATABAI:18:25-26/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r6.speaker: التفسير الكبير
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r6.claim: The Great Commentary strongly objects because the two figures do not exactly correspond and disputes a report attributed to Ali; the author answers that the discrepancy is under three months and approximation is common.
TABATABAI:18:25-26/r6.anchor: وفي التفسير الكبير شدد النكير على ذلك لعدم تطابق العددين تحقيقا

TABATABAI:18:26#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:26#3/r3.claim: A report’s claim that the duration in 18:25 is the People of the Book’s statement rejected by 18:26 is incompatible with the surrounding passage and its eloquent structure.
TABATABAI:18:26#3/r3.anchor: وقد عرفت في البيان المتقدم أن السياق يدفعه والنظم البليغ لا يقبله

TABATABAI:18:26#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r1.claim: Reports differ over whether the youths died or slept again and whether the three hundred and nine years came from God or the People of the Book; the broadly shared account is that monotheists fled a coercive polytheist king and slept in a cave.
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r1.anchor: والذي يمكن أن تعد الروايات متفقة أو كالمتفقة عليه أنهم كانوا قوما موحدين هربوا من ملك جبار

TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.claim: The cave story circulated in detailed reports from al-Qummī, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Mujāhid, Ibn Isḥāq, Wahb ibn Munabbih, and al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, among others.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.anchor: وردت قصة الكهف مفصلة كاملة في عدة روايات عن الصحابة والتابعين وأئمه أهل البيت

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.claim: The transmitted accounts disagree even on major features, while reports about dates, rulers, lineage, appearance, names, and the title أصحاب الرقيم diverge still more.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.anchor: من الاختلاف في متونها بحيث لا تكاد تتفق في جهة بارزه من جهات القصة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.claim: One cause is the story’s prominence among People of the Book: Quraysh learned it from them, and its Christian images and monuments spread it widely, so communities reshaped it to fit their beliefs.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.anchor: أن القصة مما اعتنت به أهل الكتاب كما يستفاد من رواياتها أن قريشا تلقتها عنهم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.claim: A second cause is Muslims’ broad collection of outside reports, especially through converts such as Wahb ibn Munabbih and Kaʿb al-Aḥbār; later transmitters treated such material as prophetic reports.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.anchor: اختلط بهم قوم من علماء أهل الكتاب دخلوا في الإسلام كوهب بن منبه وكعب الأحبار

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.claim: The Qurʾān selects key lessons that serve guidance instead of supplying a complete historical account; it is a book of guidance, not history.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.anchor: فما كتاب الله بكتاب تاريخ وإنما هو كتاب هدى

TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.speaker: author
